collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE X: GROWING UP, GROWING OLD AND EVERYDAY JOY (LCJ-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
The rest of the owner's 100 Living Culture ideas and the world-inspired 50: secret languages and forgotten words, coming of age, elders who will not retire, healers' oaths, failed discoveries, masks and clothes and masterpieces nobody wanted, talent shows, ridiculous hats and the day nobody worked.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A huge harvest must be divided among families with different needs: share equally, or by need.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The harvest is enormous. (subject) wants every family to get an equal share. (friend) points out that some families have eight children and some have none, and that the old widow on the hill has no one to farm for her. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: Every family gets the same. The large families are a little hungry by the end of the season; the small ones have food to spare, and most of them share it without being asked. It works out, mostly.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: Larger families and those who cannot farm get more. Some small families grumble. Nobody goes hungry. The old widow on the hill sends down a basket of her best herbs in thanks.
